subject: Brightline activation — feature commitment checklist
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Liu <sarah@brightline.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-29 09:12 -0700
Subject: Brightline activation — feature commitment checklist

Hi Sarah —

Thanks again for the sync this morning. As we discussed, Brightline wants a production-ready rollout by mid-September and has a couple of feature asks they want included in the initial activation: scoped tenant isolation for analytics exports, a short-lived KV cache bypass switch for audit-heavy requests, and a contractually-backed audit-export timeline.

I've attached a quick checklist (Brightline_MVP_requirements.xlsx) that maps each item to the teams needed and the minimal acceptance criteria. Can the product/eng leads confirm whether we can commit to the items below for a Sept 15 go-live or propose a minimal gated subset we can ship by then?

Key dates:
- Decision requested by EOD Mon 2026-08-31 (we need to communicate to Brightline for procurement timelines)
- Engineering window available: Sept 1–12 (code freeze Sept 13)

Minimal asks from Sales: clear yes/no on each item + rough engineering effort (S/M/L). If any item is blocked, please indicate mitigation (e.g., fallback config, documented limitation).

Thanks — I know this is tight.

Ava Chen
Account Exec, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

--
Ava
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava@redwood.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-29 11:03 -0700
Subject: Re: Brightline activation — feature commitment checklist

Ava / Marissa —

Thanks for the doc, looks organized. Quick read summary from Product:

1) Tenant-level analytics export isolation: feasible as a config toggle tied to per-tenant retention policies. Effort: M (2 engineers, ~1.5 weeks including QA).

2) KV cache bypass switch for specific audit requests: more invasive because of our batching assumptions; can be implemented as a request-level flag that forces synchronous path and bypasses prefix caching. Effort: L (3+ engineers, ~3 weeks).
   - Mitigation option: provide a soft SLA and an interim proxy that tags these requests and routes them to a dedicated node pool (adds infra ops overhead but faster to deploy).

3) Contractual audit-export timeline (SLA): legal needs to review retention/export guarantees. Product can document our standard timelines and offer an addendum, but export performance commitments depend on whether they need near-real-time exports or batched exports. Effort: S (docs + legal review).

We are currently capacity-constrained for the week of Sept 6 due to an internal release. If Brightline needs all three features in the initial activation window, we can propose a phased activation: tenant isolation + SLA docs for day 1, KV bypass in a canary by day 30.

I'll let Ben comment on the infra/ops feasibility and whether the proxy workaround is reasonable.

-Markus
Product Director

--

Date: 2026-08-30 10:47 -0700
Subject: Re: Brightline activation — feature commitment checklist

Folks —

Operational thoughts from infra:

- Tenant-level analytics export isolation: straightforward; we can add tenant-scoped export keys and a per-tenant worker queue. We can do this in the Sept 1–12 window if we prioritize it. Estimate: 8 dev-days + 2 QA-days + infra config.

- KV cache bypass: as Markus said, it's trickier because our continuous batching and KV cache are coupled. The fastest pragmatic approach is the proxy route: spin up an "audit" node pool that receives flagged requests via header routing and sets a small batch window (or no batch). This reduces risk to the main serving path. Rough estimate for the proxy: 10 dev-days + infra automation (helm + autoscaling). We can have an initial canary within 3 weeks, not full GA by Sept 15.

- SLA/export addendum: ops can support a documented workflow for prioritized exports, but true near-real-time guarantees require dedicated piping (webhooks or streaming export) which is outside current scope. Legal redlines (attached) will determine final wording.

Bottom line recommendation: commit to tenant-level export isolation for initial activation, provide documented SLA language for exports (non-real-time), and plan KV bypass as a short-cycle canary post-launch. This allows sales to close with a clear day-1 deliverable and a short roadmap for the remaining piece.

Ben
Engineering Lead, Platform
Redwood Inference

Attachments: legal_redline_v2.pdf

Date: 2026-08-31 16:35 -0700
Subject: Re: Brightline activation — feature commitment checklist

Sarah —

Thanks for your patience while we validated across Product and Engineering. Summary of commitments for the Sept 15 activation window: 

1) Tenant-scoped analytics export isolation: COMMITTED for day 1. Redwood will deliver tenant export keys and a scoped queue; acceptance criteria: Brightline can request and retrieve a tenant export file within documented retention bounds.

2) Audit KV-cache bypass: NOT COMMITTED for day 1. We will implement a proxy-based canary and target a limited canary release by Oct 2. For the activation, we'll offer a documented operational workaround: add a request header to mark audit flows and tag them for prioritized processing (best-effort, no hard SLA).

3) Audit-export SLA addendum: We will provide contract language describing standard export timelines (batch within 24 hours) and an optional paid add-on for prioritized streaming exports. Brightline Legal: see attached redline; please confirm whether the standard 24-hour batch timeline is acceptable or if you require a streaming addendum prior to PO.

Next steps: 
- Sarah: confirm acceptance of the day-1 commitments above by EOD 2026-09-01 so procurement can proceed.
- Marissa: I'll prepare a short activation milestone plan to include in the SOW and the project timeline.

Appreciate the coordination — we'll prioritize tenant isolation in the Sept engineering window.

Best,
Ava Chen
Account Exec, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
